content_preview.title: Decade-Old Deserialization Flaw Let Attackers Run Commands on Six Hex.pm Package Registry Servers
content_preview.summary: A parser flaw present on hex.pm since February 2016 let an unauthenticated attacker run commands on six servers; the Elixir and Erlang package registry patched it within roughly 15 minutes.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

An unauthenticated attacker ran commands on six production servers belonging to hex.pm, the package registry used by the Elixir and Erlang communities, by exploiting a parser flaw that had existed in the registry's code since February 23, 2016, according to a [security incident report](https://hex.pm/blog/security-incident-on-hexpm) published by hex.pm maintainers Peter Ullrich, Jonatan Männchen and Eric Meadows-Jönsson. editor_notes.content_quality: Clear, well-structured News piece (Overview, attack mechanism, incident response, related Ash disclosure). Technical explanation of the struct-deserialization root cause is accurate and accessible.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 5 sources read in full from decompressed .html.gz snapshots (sha256-verified against manifest; all suspicious_patterns null). Every quoted span checked character-for-character: hex.pm's postmortem quotes ('an unauthorized third party exploited...', 'The decoder rejected functions and new atoms, but it never checked maps.', 'an Elixir struct is just a map with a __struct__ key naming a module', 'no evidence of unauthorized package modifications...') all verbatim in source-0. The db_connection advisory title ('Code execution via the :log option of forged DBConnection.Stream structs in db_connection') plus GHSA ID, Nov 24 2026 publish date, and author handle 'josevalim' (José Valim) all confirmed verbatim in source-4's advisories-list rendering. The Ash CVE description quote matches source-3 verbatim (one trivial capitalization normalization at the quote boundary to fit mid-sentence grammar, standard and not corrections-worthy). Non-quoted specifics independently recomputed from source-0: 69 malicious requests, six affected servers, 18:16-18:29 UTC attack window, 18:27 firewall block, 18:30-18:31 UTC patch completion (~15 minute window), 23 releases published during the incident matched against audit logs, 62 package files and 186 registry files checksum-verified. CVSS 10.0 confirmed in source-1 and source-2. CVE-2026-133555 and db_connection fix version 2.10.3 confirmed correctly attributed to The Hacker News (source-1), not to the GitHub advisories page. Ash's affected range (3.31.3-3.37.x) and fix version (3.38.0, Nov 24) confirmed in source-3.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No fabricated specifics, no misattributed quotes, no hallucinated figures found. All numbers trace to the research the writer logged.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout; two differently-scoped facts (the unrelated Ash disclosure) correctly framed as 'a related, independently discovered' vulnerability rather than conflated with the hex.pm incident.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Herald coverage of hex.pm or this incident found (grep across src/content/articles/ for hex.pm/hexpm returned nothing).
editor_notes.overall_assessment: A rigorously sourced, accurate incident report on a critical (CVSS 10.0) decade-old deserialization flaw at a widely-used package registry, with every fact and quote independently verified against raw source text. The only automated finding (allowlist gap) has been resolved as a configuration fix, not a content issue. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, accurately verified security incident reporting for a defined Elixir/Erlang developer audience, but a contained incident with no confirmed data compromise, not broad-audience or industry-changing.
